c.tagline: A palm-fringed Gulf of Thailand island of coconut plantations, beach clubs, and Buddhist temples

card: Widely accepted at hotels and larger restaurants; cash preferred at markets and small shops

taxi.fareNote: Songthaews circle the island's main ring road on informal routes; agree the fare before boarding

emergency.note: Tourist police (1155) can assist with English-language support

walk: Chaweng and Bophut's beach strips are walkable; the island's ring road and outlying attractions require a car, scooter, or Grab

safety.safety: Generally safe island, popular with families and international tourists
safety.crime: Petty theft on crowded beaches is the main concern; scooter accidents are a more common risk than crime

hood_landmark.Chaweng: Chaweng Beach's main resort and nightlife strip
hood_landmark.Lamai: Lamai Beach's quieter resort area and Hin Ta Hin Yai rocks
hood_landmark.Bophut (Fisherman's Village): Fisherman's Village's restored wooden shophouse night market
hood_landmark.Nathon: Nathon, the island's original capital and ferry port
hood_landmark.Mae Nam: Mae Nam Beach's laid-back, family-friendly coastline

avoid.reason: Motorbike/jet-ski rental-damage scams; drink-spiking; scooter-accident risk

hood_desc: The island's busiest beach and commercial hub, with the highest concentration of hotels, restaurants, and nightlife.
A slightly quieter beach south of Chaweng, popular with a mix of families and younger travelers.
A charming restored fishing village with a popular Friday night walking market and boutique restaurants.
The original island capital and main ferry port on the west coast, more practical than picturesque.
A quiet, long beach on the north coast, popular with families and longer-stay visitors wanting fewer crowds.
lodging: Lub d Koh Samui Chaweng Beach

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water, not tap.

transit.sys: Songthaews circling the island's ring road; Grab in tourist areas
transit.pay: Cash fare or Grab app payment
transit.map: Not centrally published; songthaews run informal routes along the ring road
transit.note: Renting a scooter is common for visitors comfortable riding; songthaews and Grab otherwise cover the island

transport.air: Samui Airport (USM), with direct flights from Bangkok and some international routes
transport.bus: Combined bus-ferry tickets connect to Bangkok and other mainland cities via Surat Thani
transport.ferry: Ferries connect to Surat Thani on the mainland and to Koh Phangan and Koh Tao
transport.car: Rental cars and scooters available; the ring road circles the island

net.m: Good 4G coverage across most of the island
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: An AIS or DTAC tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory but appreciated for tour guides

food.name: Charcoal-grilled Gulf seafood
food.desc: Whole sea bass baked in a salt crust, prawns and squid grilled over coconut charcoal, served with nam jim seafood - the green chilli, lime and garlic dip.

places.name: Bangrak seafood strip
places.note: Pick your fish off the ice at 7pm and eat it grilled at a plastic table facing the water.

places.name: Ko Seng
places.note: Casual local seafood spot where freshness matters more than presentation; Thai-priced.

places.name: Baan Suan Lung Khai
places.note: Garden restaurant loved by locals for honest southern seafood cooked to traditional recipes.

food.name: Khao kluk kapi
food.desc: Rice fried in shrimp paste and served cold-plate style with sweet pork, shredded green mango, omelette ribbons, lime and raw chilli to mix in yourself.

places.name: Kapi Sator
places.note: Southern-Thai specialist built around shrimp paste and sator beans; full Thai heat as standard.

places.name: Khao Horm
places.note: Family-owned kitchen cooking southern classics from recipes passed down generations.

places.name: Nathon morning market
places.note: Island's main town market; khao kluk kapi packed in banana leaf for a few dozen baht.

food.name: Gaeng som pla
food.desc: Southern Thailand's fierce sour orange curry - fish simmered in a turmeric-and-tamarind broth with green papaya or pineapple. Fiery, thin, no coconut milk.

places.name: Baan Suan Lung Khai
places.note: Local favourite for southern fish curries and coconut-simmered squid; genuine heat levels.

places.name: Khao Horm
places.note: Balanced, aromatic southern cooking; will dial the chilli up or down if you ask.

places.name: Kapi Sator
places.note: Popular with Thai diners rather than tourists; the sour curry arrives properly sharp.

food.name: Pad sator goong
food.desc: Stink beans stir-fried hard with prawns, shrimp paste and chilli - a pungent, bitter-savoury southern plate that Thais consider the real test of a kitchen.

places.name: Kapi Sator
places.note: Named for the dish; the signature stir-fry of sator beans, prawns and shrimp paste.

places.name: Ko Seng
places.note: Simple local seafood house doing the classic version with the day's prawns.

places.name: Khao Horm
places.note: Southern staples cooked with care; good place to try sator for the first time.

food.name: Khanom jeen nam ya
food.desc: Fermented rice noodles under a fish-and-krachai curry, with a free tray of raw vegetables, pickles and boiled eggs to build your own bowl. A southern breakfast.

places.name: Nathon Sunday Walking Street
places.note: Weekly night market in the old port town, far less touristy than the Bophut market.

places.name: Laem Din Market
places.note: Samui's biggest local market; morning noodle stalls where the island actually eats breakfast.

places.name: Bophut Friday Walking Street
places.note: Island's most celebrated street-food market, roughly 5pm to 11pm every Friday.

food.name: Coconut sweets
food.desc: Samui was a coconut plantation island long before tourism: khanom tuay coconut custards, grilled coconut pancakes and coconut ice cream in the shell.

places.name: Bophut Friday Walking Street
places.note: Whole rows of coconut pancake griddles and khanom krok pans on Friday nights.

places.name: Laem Din Market
places.note: Daytime market stalls selling khanom tuay and coconut sticky rice at local prices.

places.name: Nathon Market
places.note: Old-town market where the island's traditional coconut sweets are still made daily.

food.name: Nam maprao (young coconut)
food.desc: A green coconut lopped open with a machete and drunk cold through a straw, then split so you can scrape the jelly flesh out with a spoon.

places.name: Laem Din Market
places.note: Sold by the crate at local prices, far cheaper than any beach vendor.

places.name: Bophut Fisherman's Village
places.note: Carts along the beachfront lane; also good for coconut shakes with condensed milk.

places.name: Ring Road roadside stalls
places.note: Plantation stalls all around the ring road selling straight from the trees behind them.

food.name: Cha yen
food.desc: Thai iced tea: strong orange-tinted black tea sweetened with condensed milk and poured over crushed ice, with evaporated milk swirled on top.

places.name: Laem Din Market
places.note: Tea stalls bagging cha yen to go; the local price is a fraction of the beach-bar rate.

places.name: Nathon Sunday Walking Street
places.note: Sunday-evening drinks carts with cha yen, cha manao and lime sodas.

places.name: Khao Horm
places.note: Sit-down option; sweet iced tea works well against the southern chilli heat.

landmarks: Big Buddha Temple (Wat Phra Yai)
A 12-metre golden Buddha gleams on its islet causeway, greeting arrivals by air and giving Samui its most recognisable landmark since 1972.
Wat Plai Laem
An 18-armed white Guanyin and a laughing fat Buddha rise from a lake at this vividly colourful modern temple compound near Big Buddha.
Ang Thong National Marine Park
Day cruises weave among 42 jungle-clad limestone islands with emerald lagoons and kayak caves, the archipelago that inspired The Beach.
Chaweng Beach
Samui's longest and liveliest stretch of powder-white sand curves for seven kilometres past beach clubs, resorts and buzzing nightlife.
Fisherman's Village, Bophut
Old Chinese shophouses turned boutiques and beachfront bistros host the island's beloved Friday night walking-street market.
Hin Ta and Hin Yai Rocks
These famously suggestive Grandfather and Grandmother rock formations on the Lamai coast draw giggling crowds and local legend-tellers alike.
Na Muang Waterfalls
Twin jungle cascades tumble over purple granite in Samui's lush interior, with cool plunge pools rewarding the short hike to the upper fall.
Secret Buddha Garden
High in the island's misty hills, a durian farmer's 1976 sculpture garden scatters mythic figures and shrines through tangled jungle.
Wat Khunaram
Home to the mummified monk Luang Pho Daeng, seated in meditation and sunglasses since 1973, this temple offers Samui's most singular sight.
Lad Koh Viewpoint
A roadside lookout on the Chaweng-Lamai coast road frames the classic panorama of turquoise gulf waters and palm-fringed shoreline.

train.note: There is no railway on Ko Samui. The mainland railhead is Surat Thani, about two hours away plus the ferry crossing, on the State Railway of Thailand southern line (https://www.dticket.railway.co.th/) with overnight sleepers to Bangkok. Many people buy a combined train-and-boat ticket through to the island.

bus.note: No international coaches. Combined bus-and-ferry tickets from Bangkok's Southern terminal take about 14 hours via Surat Thani and Donsak, run by Transport Co. (https://www.transport.co.th/) and Lomprayah; book through 12Go (https://12go.asia/). On the island, songthaew pickup trucks circle the ring road and are the local transport.

intl.to: Donsak, Surat Thani (Thailand) - car ferry, ~90 min
Ko Pha Ngan & Ko Tao (Thailand) - fast catamaran
Donsak & Surat Thani (Thailand) - passenger ferry with bus connection

ferry.note: There are no international sailings. The Raja and Seatran car ferries to Donsak on the mainland are the workhorses and run through the day; Lomprayah's catamarans handle the island-hopping to Pha Ngan and Tao and connect onward to Chumphon for Bangkok. Sailings are cut back or suspended in the October-December monsoon, which is the wet season on this side of the peninsula - build in a spare day before a flight.

half.name: Koh Phangan
half.blurb: A short ferry ride reaches this island known for its monthly Full Moon Party beach and quieter northern coves.

full.name: Koh Tao
full.blurb: A diving hub ringed by coral reefs and granite boulders sits farther offshore than Koh Phangan, reached by high-speed catamaran.
